posts.subject: Re:Monitor menu options locked e.g. brightness, color + other (lenovo legion pro 27Q-10)
posts.author: Adriel_lenovo
posts.message_html:
Hello and welcome to the Lenovo Community purple240,

I understand you're having trouble accessing the monitor settings of your Lenovo Legion Pro 27Q-10 monitor. May I ask first, what joystick are you using to access the monitor settings? Is it the built-in controls to access the OSD menu?

Based on your description, it seems that your monitor’s OSD (joystick) menu is being restricted by the current signal mode or by another enabled monitor feature, which can make items like Brightness unavailable.

Please follow this single path in order:

1) Power-reset the monitor (clears many OSD lock states)
- Turn the monitor off.
- Unplug the monitor power cable from the wall.
- Wait 60 seconds.
- Plug it back in and turn it on.

2) Make sure you’re adjusting settings while a supported video signal is active
- Connect a device that is actively outputting video (PC/laptop/console) and make sure you can see the desktop/game.
- If you’re on a console, open the console Home screen (not a “no signal” screen).
- Then open the OSD again and check if Brightness becomes selectable.

3) Switch to a different picture mode/preset (common reason Brightness is locked)
- Using the joystick, go to the monitor’s Picture/Preset settings.
- Change the preset (for example from a gaming/HDR/special mode to a Standard/Custom mode).
- After switching the preset, check Brightness again.

4) Temporarily disable HDR / special dynamic features (these often lock Brightness)
- In the OSD, look for items such as HDR, Dynamic Contrast, Eye Care/Low Blue Light, or similar “enhancement” features.
- Turn them Off (temporarily) and re-check if Brightness becomes adjustable.
- If you are using Windows: go to Settings > System > Display and toggle “Use HDR” Off to test.

5) Try another input and cable (rules out signal-format limitations)
- Switch from HDMI to DisplayPort (or another HDMI port) if available.
- Use a different cable if possible.
- Re-test the OSD Brightness control.

6) Factory reset the monitor settings
- In the OSD, find Reset / Factory Reset / Recall and perform the reset.
- After reset, re-check Brightness.

7) Update monitor firmware
- Click here to download the necessary firmware/driver for the monitor.

Let us know how it goes.

Thanks,
Adriel_Lenovo
